question: Where can I get the locations of known mineral deposits and occurrences in Spain, with commodity, size or grade, and status (explored, mined, abandoned)?

answer.summary: IGME’s BDMIN catalogues Spanish mineral occurrences and operations using point layers with commodity, size-class and status fields. Operators publish tonnage and grade for selected projects; MSP-REFRAM offers historical data for selected refractory metals. BDMIN record queries and completeness could not be verified.
main_caveats: The inventory contains recorded occurrences, not proof that every deposit is known or commercially viable.
Layer descriptions and fields were inspected; record counts, individual values and coordinate quality were not verified.
Status and size classes can be historical; confirm the observation date before treating them as current.
Do not treat a qualitative size class as measured tonnage or ore grade.
The occurrence layer metadata has an anomalous southern extent of 3.675° N; affected records could not be identified.
answer.confidence_reason: Descriptions and schema were inspected, but data queries and completeness could not be verified.

how_to_use.example_result: Layer metadata reports esriGeometryPoint, EPSG:4326 and fields Codigo_indicio, Nombre_mina, X, Y, Tamaño_indicio and Sustancia. No data records were retrieved.
steps: Inspect the occurrence layer metadata and the industrial workings layer metadata at https://mapas.igme.es/gis/rest/services/BasesDatos/IGME_BDMIN_Explotaciones/MapServer/0.
The catalogue links the corresponding ArcGIS REST services; both have two scale-dependent display layers.
A record query and pagination remain unverified; do not assume that layer metadata alone proves the public features can be retrieved.
reading_traps: A point indicates a recorded location, not the full deposit footprint.
The size field is a class, not necessarily ore tonnage or grade.
The same features may be represented in the two scale-dependent layers; avoid combining them without checking identifiers.

The layer metadata advertises YMin 3.675255509 in EPSG:4326, far south of Spain; record queries failed, so the number and identity of affected points cannot be established. Check coordinates before use.

how_to_use.example_result: Puerto Piedrafita 1: BDMIN 78002, Estado Abandonada, Sustancias Marmol, UTMX 288.152, UTMY 4.766.620, Huso 30, Fecha 02/09/2009. Second volume page 4: PAZ II, Cuarcita, Activa intermitente, 19/03/2015.
steps: Open the regional inventory page and select the PDF volume by map number; one sheet occupies each PDF page.
Extract the labelled fields and keep survey date and BDMIN identifier.
Interpret UTM coordinates in ED50 and zone 30 as labelled on the sheet; transform the CRS only with an appropriate datum transformation.
Second volume page 4 was checked at https://info.igme.es/cartografiadigital/datos/rocasindustriales/pdfs/CastillaLeon_InventarioExplotaciones/0101-0200.pdf.
reading_traps: The two checked sheets have observation dates in 2009 and 2015; status is historical, not necessarily current.
UTMX and UTMY use periods as thousands separators; they are ED50 coordinates, not WGS84.
Pit dimensions on a mine sheet are not deposit size, resource quantity or grade.
One checked coordinate converts from ED50 UTM 30N to approximately 43.020855, -5.601255, about 1.6 km from the Piedrafita discharge point; this is a plausibility check, not boundary validation.

recipe: Search BOE by the deposit or mine name, then open the actual notice or law.
In the preamble of Real Decreto-ley 6/2014, record Aznalcóllar, commodity, 35 million tonnes confirmed and 45 million tonnes probable, the document date and the stated historical activity condition.
Preserve the distinction between confirmed reserves and probable resources; this one document does not establish present status or coverage of other deposits.
For a regional match in Castilla y León, use the map-number / BDMIN correlation to choose the numbered PDF and extract one labelled sheet per page.
On page 1 record Puerto Piedrafita 1, its BDMIN code, rock, abandoned status, ED50 zone and observation date; preserve the status as historical.
if_unstructured.location_method: Use the corresponding IGME point where its identity is independently matched; the example decree does not give point coordinates.
